reason: is_usage(code, field) is the one rule in L1.registry, L2.destructive-half, the stateless test and the L2.input answers; mutants that ignore the field, accept a reserved code, a document-declared code or any exit, drop OPTION_INVALID from the registry filter or leave the stateless test's field unfiltered all fail (atip_checkl2safety_04, atip_checkl2input_07, 13, atip_checkl1_04); a mutant that lets a non-reserved INPUT_* name through survives (note recorded)
summary: Differs from checker.md 1.3.1 section 2 (ATIP feedback): 'USAGE stands for USAGE or its registered finer replacement: a registered exit-2 code the tool uses instead of USAGE, whose field names an argument'. Only L2.input-usage (input.rs:303-305) applies that; the shared is_usage (checks/l1.rs:157), used by L1.registry, L2.destructive-half (safety.rs:336), the stateless test and L2.input-pointer/-conflict answers, accepts exactly UNKNOWN_OPTION and OPTION_REQUIRED (the two codes of atip 1.2.1 7.2.2), ignores field and does not know OPTION_INVALID, which checker.md names. So a 1.3-style tool that registers OPTION_INVALID passes L2.input-usage and fails L2.destructive-half. Canon's claim is 1.2 and its own tool uses USAGE, so nothing fails today; either make is_usage take (code, field) or say in checker.md that the finer codes are the claim's.
